text: The Race: what kind of shoe is this?

bank.q: A sturdy leather shoe decorated with rows of little punched holes
A slip-on leather shoe with no laces, often with a 'penny' strap across the top
A summer shoe with a canvas top and a sole of woven rope
A soft leather slip-on first made by Native Americans
A high heel as thin as a dagger
A waterproof rubber boot named after a duke
A shoe carved from a single block of wood, loved in the Netherlands
A rubber sandal held on by a strap between the toes
A backless shoe that slides on at the front, sharing its name with a farm animal
A simple canvas gym shoe with a rubber sole, once a PE-lesson staple
An ankle boot with elastic panels at the sides, loved by the Beatles
A suede ankle boot with two eyelets and a crepe sole, made famous by Clarks
A women's shoe held on by a strap around the back of the heel
A short, slim heel made famous by Audrey Hepburn
A heel that runs solid under the whole length of the foot
The classic plain office heel with no straps or laces
A flat, slipper-like women's shoe inspired by dancers
A shoe or boot with a very long, sharply pointed toe, loved by 1950s rockers
A shoe with a thick crepe sole, worn by Teddy Boys and later by punks
A rounded, low-heeled shoe with a single strap across the top of the foot, often worn by girls

text: The Race: which British bird is this?

bank.q: Red breast, sings all winter, and follows gardeners for worms
Black and white with a long tail: 'one for sorrow, two for joy'
Electric blue and orange, it dives into rivers for fish
A seabird with a colourful striped beak, nicknamed the 'sea parrot'
A tiny brown bird with a cocked-up tail and a very loud song
A small garden bird with a blue cap and a yellow front
Red face and a flash of yellow on the wings; a group is a 'charm'
A glossy, speckled bird whose huge flocks swirl in a 'murmuration'
A tall grey bird that stands stock-still at the water's edge, waiting for fish
Lays its eggs in other birds' nests and is named after its call
A pale, heart-faced owl that hunts silently over fields at dusk
A small falcon often seen hovering over motorway verges
A fork-tailed summer visitor that nests in barns; one doesn't make a summer
A colourful crow with a blue wing flash that buries acorns
Green with a red cap; its laughing call is known as a 'yaffle'
A huge white bird with an orange beak; the unmarked ones on open water belong to the monarch
A black and white shore bird with a long orange-red beak and a loud piping call
A russet bird of prey with a forked tail, brought back to Gateshead's Derwent valley
A big white seabird that plunges into the sea like a dart, famous on the Bass Rock
A speckled bird that smashes snail shells on a stone 'anvil'
